notes: Three articles read: the Uniqlo opening, the Doolan-Larson conversion and the weekly food column. The food roundup's SF items were extracted as separate findings. No sfist items file on this branch records any of these three URLs, so all three are first reads here.

findings.address_as_written: the former Old Navy space on Market Street
findings.description: Uniqlo is set to open a new two-story, 20,315-square-foot store in the former Old Navy space on Market Street by October 9, returning downtown more than five years after closing its Powell Street flagship in 2021. It would be the brand's second San Francisco store alongside Stonestown Galleria, with a Re.Uniqlo Studio for tailoring and repairs.

citation.label: SFist, “Uniqlo to Open In Former Old Navy Site on Market Street In Early October,” 19 September 2026

raw.text: a new two-story store in the former Old Navy space on Market Street

findings.note: The article gives no numbered address.

publish.note: One event, one entry. /san-francisco/south-of-market/market-street/801/ already carries this opening from Hoodline, dated 2026-09-14 — a story that does print the numbered address SFist's account leaves out.

findings.address_as_written: the Doolan-Larson Building, corner of Haight and Ashbury streets
findings.description: San Francisco Heritage is partnering with Seattle's KEXP radio station and the Blue Bear School of Music to turn the historic Doolan-Larson Building at Haight and Ashbury into a music and culture center with a rooftop concert venue, broadcast facilities and music education. Early plans by Gensler and Page & Turnbull call for a contemporary addition above the three Haight Street retail spaces; KEXP anticipates construction costs exceeding the $16 million it raised for its Seattle facility. SF Heritage has owned the property since 2017, when it was donated by its longtime owner; its artist-in-residence program will end.

extra.partners: SF Heritage, KEXP, Blue Bear School of Music
extra.owner_since_2017: San Francisco Heritage (donated by longtime owner)

citation.label: SFist, “Haight-Ashbury Landmark to Become New Music and Culture Center,” 18 September 2026

raw.text: The historic Doolan-Larson Building on the corner of Haight and Ashbury streets is set for a new chapter as San Francisco Heritage works with Seattle’s KEXP independent radio station and SF’s Blue Bear School of Music to transform the property into a cultural and music center

findings.note: The building is identified by name and intersection; no numbered address is given.

publish.note: One event, one entry. /san-francisco/haight-ashbury/haight-street/1500/ already carries this conversion from the San Francisco Chronicle, dated 2026-09-17. SFist's account names the building and the intersection but no street number, so it could not have been placed on its own in any case.

publish.note: The headline is the entry, and this one would describe the wrong building: “Buzzy Coffee and Pizza In the Avenues” is a claim about the Richmond and the Sunset, and 149 New Montgomery is in SoMa. news/AGENTS.md forbids editing a headline to fit, so the entry is unusable — the same call as 2026-08-25-0007. raw.text: will take over the former Reliable Rexall pharmacy space at 801 Irving Street in the Inner Sunset, with a goal to open by mid-2027.

findings.note: Dated to publication, not the mid-2027 target opening: the target is a forecast, not an event that has happened, and dating the entry to it would misrepresent a not-yet-open business as this building's most recent news a year from now. Same call as the L'Amourette finding in this batch (2026-09-20-hl-0003), which uses the article date for the same reason.

resolution.method: EAS exact match on 801 IRVING ST → parcel 1764001; sf-parcels has blklot 1764001 active, 1307–1317 09TH; the 2025 roll records it as commercial retail, built 1912. EAS puts 801, 815, 821, 825, 827 IRVING ST on that parcel, so per the directory contract the fact belongs on one page at the lowest, 801. The address carries no parcel number in EAS; the active parcel its coordinates fall in is 1764001.

publish.note: Published on /san-francisco/inner-sunset/9th-avenue/1307/ as sfist-2026-09-18, and on the homepage news grid. The address resolves to this page's parcel by point (EAS carries no parcel number for 801 Irving Street); the page already existed, so no seeding and no manifest. Nothing for the building block: the article names a planned new tenant, not a fact about the structure.
